dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The West-dealer subset contains 90 annual-plan rows, all from DLR-104 or DLR-219" and cites `recharges.csv`, `term_days=365`, and the dealer filter.

"The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags" and identifies `dealer_import_log.csv`, DF-00020/DF-00040, and the relevant fields.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31-May cluster represents scheduled batch-posting timing by two West dealers, not duplicate transactions."
"The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date," with the claim compared against observed lag data.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I tested the email assertions against the data (and explicitly flagged what is untestable) rather than accepting them as proof."
"Entitlement Activation: We do not know if the 90 annual renewals activated subscriber entitlements."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is a targeted, read-only query" that is described as "cheap and fully reversible."
"If policy requires effective-date reporting, escalate that specific presentation issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: No material irregularity detected; do not escalate or alter existing postings."
The submission provides an evidence table, rejected hypotheses, unknowns, decision-changing evidence, and a concrete safe next action.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "All source events are unique and cash reconciles to the ledger with zero variance, showing no evidence of fake revenue." Unique source_event_id values and cash reconciliation reduce duplicate-revenue risk but do not by themselves establish that revenue is genuine or that entitlements were delivered.

"Pipeline defect: rejected because `dealer_import_log.csv` shows 41/41 files as `RECONCILED` with accepted rows perfectly matching received rows and no key field nulls." These checks support successful ingestion and reconciliation but do not fully rule out every pipeline defect, including incorrect transformations or downstream date handling.

"Backdating or period-stuffing: rejected" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants; matching effective and posted months and dates spread across 1–28 May reduce that hypothesis but do not conclusively exclude manipulation or contractual noncompliance.

The recommendation to close the anomaly if policy permits posting-date reporting is made while entitlement activation remains untested, although the submission appropriately identifies this as decision-changing evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled duplicate billing, fictitious billing, backdating, and ingestion failure as alternatives, and it recognized event-time distortion in downstream analytics. The strongest insufficiently tested alternative is a provisioning or entitlement defect: the 90 financially reconciled renewals might still fail to activate subscriber entitlements. A secondary unresolved alternative is a policy or contractual breach caused by monthly batching even if no duplicate revenue exists.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and document the read-only entitlement reconciliation for the 90 renewals, alongside an explicit duplicate-cash-to-entitlement join, before definitively closing the anomaly; then make `effective_event_date` the default date for downstream event-time analytics while retaining `posted_at` for posting-control reporting.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell to index 59 in June, while E (101), N (101), and W (96) controls held flat."
"Pre-auth terminations tripled: 24.0% (NOVA) vs 7.9% (LEGACY). Auth error codes hit 13.4%."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The containment dashboard artificially inflates success rates by actively excluding early-stage drop-offs."
"reconciling IVR sessions to CareDesk cases reveals that LEGACY sessions generated tickets 49.5% of the time (219/442), whereas NOVA-S1 created tickets for only 3.3% of sessions (90/2,709)."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The massive surge in pre-auth failures represents frustrated customers whose complaints were systematically prevented from becoming logged CareDesk cases."

"This massive structural collapse in case creation, combined with a cross-channel drop ... confirms that measurement artifacts and authentication failures cause the bulk of the decline, with genuine self-service for basic intents causing the remainder."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT expand nationally. Keep the South pilot running (reversible)."

"Add pre-auth abandonment and all-contact containment to the dashboard, reconcile IVR sessions to CareDesk cases, fix the auth/prompt defects, and re-evaluate over two full weeks against an E/N/W control before any rollout decision."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The 7-day repeat-contact / callback rate for South customers (the decisive CX signal)."
"When a session ends at authenticate with an error ... what happens to that issue operationally—is any case, callback, or queue entry created, and where is it logged?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that the decline is "predominantly a measurement artifact" and that pre-auth failures represent "frustrated customers" is not established without linked journey outcomes or sampled call review; abandonment and authentication failure are not themselves complaints.
The statement that 175 subscribers were "never seen again" in the two files does not establish their operational outcome or absence from other channels.

The wording that the evidence "confirms" the causal mix of measurement artifact, authentication failures, and genuine deflection is too strong for observational data with the repeat-contact and case-fate fields still unknown.
The claim that NOVA "logs ~12x more sessions" is inconsistent with the quoted counts of 2,709 NOVA sessions versus 442 LEGACY sessions, which is approximately 6.1x.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately preserves genuine self-service deflection as an alternative, citing new balance-check and pack-information stages, but it does not adequately preserve the possibility that some pre-auth abandonment was benign or unrelated to complaint intent. Those stages also show IVR behavior, not completed customer outcomes.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete subscriber-level journey linkage and sampled call listening for pre-auth failures, repeat contacts, transfers, and case creation across channels before labeling abandonment as failed CX or estimating genuine deflection.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` and specific fields: `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `severity`, `duration_min`, `timestamp_local`, and `inverter_id`.
It distinguishes observations from inference by stating that constant zero-impact fields “cannot guarantee the telemetry is actively computed.”

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It rejects the equipment-breakdown hypothesis by cross-checking event wording against zero impact, cleared status, short duration, and lack of recurrence.

It also considers an innocent data-scope explanation and proposes a read-only unfiltered export query. The main limitation is that the reasoning remains within one export rather than triangulating against an independent operational channel.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the completeness concern as a “data-scope check, not evidence of equipment breakdown.”
It explicitly qualifies the zero-impact conclusion because the field “could simply be unpopulated,” and gives conditional next steps if additional faults or nonzero-impact events appear.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check” is proportionate to four short, cleared, zero-impact events.
The proposed read-only query without status filters is a targeted, low-cost test that could change the decision while preserving the operational constraint against unnecessary escalation.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion appropriately avoids inventing a plant problem from communication warnings, recognizes zero MW impact and quick recovery, and stops after a narrowly scoped completeness check if no contrary records appear.
This matches the strongest supported interpretation while retaining a limited data-quality qualification.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “This provides zero escalation signal” is slightly stronger than the evidence warrants because the submission itself notes that `impact_mw` might be unpopulated; “no observed escalation signal in this export” would be more precise.

The conditional instruction to “stop the review entirely” is reasonable here but should be understood as stopping this investigative thread, not proving unit health or data completeness beyond the verified query.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, so the four benign-looking records may not represent all events in the period. A secondary possibility is that `impact_mw` is a constant or uncomputed field; neither possibility, however, establishes physical equipment failure without additional evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed unfiltered read-only query and verify both row coverage and whether `impact_mw` is populated or derived; if practical, compare any returned events with an independent SCADA/availability record before closing the review.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission reproduces the headline calculation using `dispatch_blocks.csv`: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%.”
It explicitly identifies the cross-day comparison and cites the eight daily penalty totals grouped from `dispatch_blocks.csv`.

It constructs the same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source`, reporting Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086 and approximately 17.6%.
It distinguishes observed penalty arithmetic from causal interpretation and identifies missing commercial-settlement evidence in `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the central comparison problem by noting that 31.6% compares 29 May with 28 May, while daily penalties vary substantially.
It performs the required same-day counterfactual rather than simply rejecting the pilot: “the stronger same-day modeled estimate is about 17.6%.”
It considers plausible non-causal explanations and limitations, including “Forecast skill vs hindsight” and differences across wind regimes.
It cross-checks commercial interpretation by separating DSM penalties from energy revenue and notes that net value is not established.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion is explicitly scoped: “neither estimate establishes a general causal effect.”
The submission labels the 17.6% result “descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”
It identifies specific decision-changing unknowns: immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net-settlement modeling.
It avoids overcorrecting to no value, retaining the narrower claim that the submitted schedule had a modeled penalty lower than the retained base schedule on 29 May.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to keep the pilot at its current scope and not expand yet follows from the absence of controlled causal and net-value evidence.
The proposed next test is prospective and discriminating: “pre-registered matched high-wind stow days,” immutable pre-submission timestamps, and net commercial settlement calculations.
The action preserves the operational pilot while using a read-only shadow calculation, rather than making an unsupported expansion or termination decision.
It specifies how results would affect expansion: consistent within-day net-positive cashflows would support expansion, while failure to replicate would argue against it.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The headline is accurately retained as “the descriptive 28-to-29 May difference,” not a causal estimate.
The submission correctly preserves the smaller same-day modeled benefit: “17.6% only as the modeled one-day estimate.”

Its overall conclusion—insufficient evidence that the pilot caused a 31.6% improvement while retaining the pilot at current scope—matches the strongest supported interpretation of the supplied evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Post-hoc adjustments invalidate the AI claim” is somewhat absolute; post-hoc timing would invalidate a predictive-skill or causal attribution claim, but could still leave an operational optimization observation.

“Net negative cashflows or failure to replicate would conclude the pilot” is stronger than necessary for a single prospective test; failure should more cautiously trigger reassessment or continued hold rather than automatically conclude the pilot.

The 17.6% counterfactual relies on treating the retained base schedule as the relevant same-day benchmark; the submission appropriately calls it modeled, but could state this counterfactual assumption more explicitly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May schedule may have performed better than the retained base schedule in the modeled calculation, but the improvement could reflect day-specific wind conditions, forecast or schedule-selection differences, or the construction of the base counterfactual rather than pilot efficacy. The 31.6% result is primarily a favorable day-to-day comparison against an unusually high-penalty 28 May.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the prospective test explicitly pre-registered with a defined counterfactual or randomized/shadow comparison and quantify uncertainty around the 17.6% estimate, while retaining the proposed timestamp and net-settlement checks.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The declared code `90211000` is the approved code for P1001 in Switzerland, effective 2025-01-01." — `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`, Swiss Matrix tab
"The flag expected `90211090`, but this is the Helios code, which is \"migration-mapped\" and \"not customs-ruling status\"." — `product_master_current.xlsx`, Read Me tab
"The automated schema completely fails to model `code-system identifier`, `nomenclature version`, or `effective dates`." — `canonical-schema-v0.3.md`, \"Not yet modeled\" section
"We lack the explicit Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected because `90211000` is the exact jurisdiction-correct code approved in the Swiss tariff matrix; the 8-digit difference represents a legitimate cross-system variation (Swiss vs EU/Helios), not a typo."
"Rejected because the product master's Read Me explicitly warns that the Helios code is commercial master data and \"not customs-ruling status\"."

"If a Tares extract confirms `90211000`, it confirms the non-escalation decision and we close the flag. If it mandates a different 8-digit suffix, it would overturn the decision and trigger a formal escalation."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Confidence" is explicitly assigned to each evidence claim, including "Medium" for the cross-jurisdiction matching statement.
"Missing Evidence" identifies the absent "Binding Legal Authority" and specifies how either possible Tares outcome would affect the decision.
"Do NOT escalate this packet as a likely declaration error" is qualified by a reversible hold and a request for official Swiss Tares confirmation.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Both codes share the exact same harmonized 6-digit root (`902110`), differing only in their jurisdiction-specific national digits."
"Cross-jurisdiction string matching is \"not expected\"; codes only match at the HS6 root (`902110`)."
"The automated schema completely fails to model `code-system identifier`, `nomenclature version`, or `effective dates`."
"This mismatch is a cross-code-system false positive caused by a schema design gap, not a broker error."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible hold on the flag and request the official Swiss Tares confirmation for P1001."
"If it confirms `90211000`, close the flag as a cross-nomenclature false positive"
"If it mandates a different 8-digit suffix, it would overturn the decision and trigger a formal escalation."
"Update the comparator tool to normalize codes to their HS6 root before flagging."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declared code `90211000` matches the approved Swiss local tariff code" is supported by the matrix but not yet by binding Swiss Tares evidence; the submission appropriately acknowledges this limitation.

"This mismatch is a cross-code-system false positive caused by a schema design gap, not a broker error" is a well-supported working conclusion, but the absence of the official Tares entry means broker error is not conclusively excluded.

"Update the comparator tool to normalize codes to their HS6 root before flagging" could be unsafe if implemented as a blanket suppression rule, because legitimate national tariff distinctions may require review beyond HS6 matching.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix could be stale, misapplied to P1001, or non-authoritative, and the declaration could therefore still have an incorrect national suffix despite the Helios Read Me warning. The missing Swiss Tares extract is the decisive unresolved evidence, and the submission correctly identifies that possibility.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the official Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001, then define comparator logic that preserves jurisdiction, nomenclature version, and effective-date metadata rather than using HS6 normalization as a blanket no-flag rule.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the declaration facts to "`declaration.pdf`, IE-2025-000411, Line 1" and the missing support to "`review_note.txt`, Complete text."
It identifies the relevant register record and dates: "`supplier_origin_register.csv`, P1006 rows, SUP-02 fields; `declaration.pdf`, declaration date."
It states the register limitation using the cited reference: "no document found in the register 'does not prove that no document exists outside the register.'"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests and rejects the proposition that "Preference=Yes proves the claim is fully supported" because the indicator is only a declaration field and "no supporting declaration is actually linked."
It distinguishes unsupported evidence from fraud: "The evidence reaches 'unsupported,' not 'fraud.'"
It tests the expired-record hypothesis against dates: "its `2025-07-31` end date versus the `2025-09-18` entry date."
It identifies alternative sourcing and document-location hypotheses, including "SUP-03/05/06" and evidence "outside the incomplete register."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion is expressly limited: "currently NOT supported" and "'unsupported' is not the same as 'proven false.'"
The submission acknowledges that the register is incomplete and that its silence "does not prove that a document doesn't exist outside of it."
It labels the alternative supplier-link evidence "Low" confidence and identifies the actual supplier, rule, and external-document status as unresolved.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: It correctly distinguishes manufacturing country from preferential origin: "the workshop says manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."
It identifies a data-lineage failure: "the ClearView record lacks any linked supplier declaration" and the airway bill "provides no supplier_id."
It recognizes system coverage limitations: "the register is incomplete" and documents may exist "outside the register."
The explanation is sound but does not fully describe how the declaration, ClearView, procurement records, and register should be reconciled or how preference rules would be validated operationally.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended control is proportionate and reversible: "place a reversible administrative hold" and "request the document, rather than jumping to a formal fraud referral."
The proposed verification is targeted: "provide the active supplier declaration and the originating rule for the actual supplier."
It conditions escalation appropriately: "Escalate to a formal error/fraud referral only if this manual verification is requested and subsequently fails."

However, it states "Treat the line as non-preferential (MFN) for now, which is 0.0% and duty-neutral" without establishing from the cited materials that the applicable MFN rate is 0.0%; the declaration's 0.0% rate does not by itself prove the non-preferential rate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Treat the line as non-preferential (MFN) for now, which is 0.0% and duty-neutral" is not adequately supported unless the applicable tariff schedule independently confirms a 0.0% MFN rate.

"If tied to SUP-01 (US), it would mandate non-preferential treatment" is directionally plausible but should be stated conditionally on the applicable preferential rule and verified supplier/origin evidence.
"Withdraw or correct the preference indicator if no valid proof is produced" may require following the applicable customs correction procedure; the submission does not cite that procedural basis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid despite the incomplete ClearView/register packet: the shipment could have been supplied by SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or a valid supplier declaration may exist in Procurement's category folders. The evidence therefore supports a documentation gap and temporary verification hold, not a finding that the preference claim is false or fraudulent.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the applicable MFN tariff rate and customs-correction procedure, while linking IE-2025-000411 to the actual supplier and retrieving the supplier declaration and qualifying rule before asserting duty-neutral non-preferential treatment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"The SOP requires measuring from 'evidence available' ... this extract lacks an exact evidence_available_ts field"
"All 42 open HOLD batches ... were received on or after 24 July"
"17 rows with COA MISSING and 13 with INDEX_PENDING are likely artifacts of the nightly-index lag"

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning

"Measuring cycle time on only the completed rows creates severe right-censoring and survivorship bias"
"Missing COAs prove a compliance breach ... requires live-portal verification"

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Confidence" table labels the timestamp, SOP-exception, and HOLD claims as High
"If this check returns varied intraday operational times, it proves the extract is defaulting to the snapshot boundary"
"17 rows ... are likely artifacts of the nightly-index lag"

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not launch the 'day and a half' KPI yet"
"The limitation is semantic alignment with the SOP clock rather than data corruption"
"Smallest verification: Run a read-only live-QCore spot-check for 5-10 batches"

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "'1.5 days is a trustworthy cycle time.' Rejected because ... wrong start clock ... 02:10 timestamps ... and ... complex exceptions"
"'Missing COAs prove a compliance breach.' Rejected because this status aligns ... with the known nightly-index lag"
"'Discard the extract as corrupt.' Rejected because duration arithmetic is valid and monotonic"

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live-QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows"
"evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping"
"Follow the 42 HOLD rows to disposition"
"Same-day CertVault/QCore reconciliation"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The conclusion that 02:10:00 values are "fabricated daily snapshot defaults" is stronger than the evidence supports; the concentration and schedule match establish an important anomaly, but not whether the values are defaults, batched operational releases, or interface commit timestamps.

A varied live-QCore time for sampled rows would show that the extract timestamp does not represent the live operational event time, but by itself would not prove the precise defaulting mechanism or fully invalidate every possible KPI use.
The statement that COA statuses "align perfectly" with the CertVault lag and are likely artifacts is plausible but not demonstrated without same-day record-level reconciliation.

The claimed median of approximately 21.3 hours is not fully traceable because the submission says there is no exact evidence_available_ts field and does not identify the proxy field and calculation used.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration may reflect an interface commit or batch-release process rather than fabricated data. The extract may therefore contain valid system timestamps but still be unsuitable for the SOP KPI because they measure interface timing rather than the decision or evidence-availability event. A further alternative is that the QCore and LabTrack/other source extracts are not a coherent point-in-time snapshot, so end-to-end durations and status joins may mix different system states.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize obtaining the event/decision timestamp definition and a short event-log extract linking evidence availability, release decision, and QCore interface commit for sampled batches, with source-extract timestamps. This would discriminate workflow delay from interface timing and address the non-coherent-snapshot risk more directly than a live spot-check alone.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Open requests total $166,495.60 (`qty × external_quote_usd`)" and "8 actionable... 12... Needs check... 4... Not transferable"; these are tied to `part_requests.csv` and specific candidate rows, but the calculation and joins are not shown.
"MaintStar-global is 2026-06-26, ~4 weeks older than ProcureNet"; tied to `source_freshness.csv` and appropriately linked to the need for live confirmation.
"HA-0022 has on-hand 3 but available -1"; triangulated across `spare_parts.csv` and `maintenance_email.txt`.

The submission names relevant restrictions and fields such as revision, qualification, reservation, and availability, but does not explicitly evidence UOM handling or show the restriction rows for each actionable match.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "I advise against converting semantic-search hits into automatic transfers" correctly separates retrieval from transfer authorization.

"available_qty_global = -1 means zero stock" is rejected using the independent on-hand evidence for HA-0022, and "Same part family means interchangeable" is rejected using the rev-A versus rev-B case.

"The real problem is master-data hygiene, not search recall" is a stronger causal conclusion than the evidence establishes: blank MPNs demonstrate an identity-data problem, but do not show that semantic retrieval is unnecessary or that search recall is not also material.

The submission generally distinguishes exact identity, revision, reservation, and freshness constraints, but it does not fully explain the mechanism by which the counts and dollar categories were derived.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Actionable transfers require live CMMS confirmation" appropriately downgrades conclusions because `MaintStar-global` is stale.
The table labels uncertain cases "Needs check" and identifies identity, revision, split-stock, and availability uncertainties.
"Only 2 free rev-B VLV-3722 units exist vs 4 units of rev-B demand" is marked Medium confidence, showing some source-quality calibration.

The claim that an exact MPN join "resolves the 13 identified requests immediately" is insufficiently qualified because exact identity alone does not establish current transferability, UOM, or all restriction conditions.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I advise against converting semantic-search hits into automatic transfers" is a useful safety-preserving decision rather than blind adoption of search results.
The split into "Actionable now," "Needs check," and "Not transferable" provides operational prioritization and separates candidate value from immediately actionable value.
The requested live CMMS, engineering sign-off, and local-record checks are reversible safeguards.
The recommendation lacks an explicit small pilot, owner, timing, or success criteria for using semantic search as candidate generation, so it does not fully turn the analysis into a learning loop.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every semantic-search hit should be transferred" is rejected using MPN, revision, and truly-free-stock requirements.
"available_qty_global = -1 means zero stock" is tested against on-hand quantity and reservation lag.
"Same part family means interchangeable" is rejected with the valve revision mismatch, and pulling reserved MTR-4401 drives is rejected using reservation and safety-criticality evidence.

The competing interpretation that semantic search remains valuable for generating candidates for the 11 blank-MPN requests is not directly tested or rejected; the submission instead asserts that completing identifiers is preferable.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "MPN/revision from local records" is a targeted request for the 11 blank-MPN identities.
"Free stock for HA-0022/ME-0006: Live CMMS query" directly addresses stale or contradictory availability.
"Rev A vs B compatibility: Engineer sign-off" targets the key technical decision right.
"Global snapshot freshness: Live CMMS query" addresses temporal inconsistency, although the submission does not prioritize these requests by decision impact or identify a single accountable owner.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The real problem is master-data hygiene, not search recall" is not established by the evidence; the data supports an identity-quality problem but does not show semantic search has no useful role.

"An exact join on manufacturer_part_no ... resolves the 13 identified requests immediately" overstates what an exact identity join proves. It can identify candidates, but revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, current availability, and site restrictions still govern transferability.

"The remaining 11 require completing blank identifiers, not an expensive semantic search" treats semantic search as unnecessary without testing whether it can efficiently generate candidate identities for those blank-MPN requests.
UOM handling is not explicitly evidenced despite the stated policy constraints.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search is still valuable as a controlled candidate-generation tool for blank or inconsistent MPN requests, while exact MPN matches remain stronger identity evidence. The appropriate conclusion is not to reject semantic search, but to prevent its hits from becoming transfers until engineering, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and live-availability checks pass.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small, reversible validation on the 11 blank-MPN requests: use semantic search to generate ranked candidates, have stores or engineering verify MPN/revision/UOM and restrictions, and query live CMMS for availability. Compare precision, verification time, and confirmed transferable value against identifier-only triage; use the result to decide whether semantic search adds value beyond master-data cleanup.
